assumptions: The zero-cost guard is evaluated during limit order matching before completion.
The report's 'should trigger only when' is read as: guard triggering requires the one-side-receives-without-sending condition.

unresolved.description: The report does not quote the exact zero-cost check expression or its operands, so the guard's internal numeric relation cannot be encoded beyond the grounded Boolean 'one_side_receives_without_sending'.
The report does not state whether matched base/quote amounts are caller-supplied inputs or derived from order state, so the disjoint-bits fact is encoded as a single grounded Boolean.

limitations: The impact text describes scope (all limit order matching, partial and full) rather than an explicit revert verb; the revert outcome is encoded as the report-claimed failure of legitimate matching.
Fill orders are stated to be unaffected; that exclusion is not part of this claim's formula.
